pitch: When you can’t pick up, people on your site still leave a name. It hits the phone you actually look at. They’re not told they’re booked. You call. We install it on the site you already have — looks like your page — and we don’t leave until you called a test lead. Seventy-five hundred, one time. We don’t answer the phone for you.
pitchEs: Cuando no puedes contestar, la gente en tu página deja nombre y teléfono. Te llega al correo o WhatsApp que sí revisas. No les decimos que ya tienen cita. Tú los llamas. Lo instalamos en la web que ya tienes, con tu mismo estilo, y no nos vamos hasta que tú llamaste un pedido de prueba. Siete mil quinientos, una vez. Nosotros no contestamos el teléfono por ti.
collect:
1. Live website URL
2. Shop name
3. Owner cell
4. Who can edit the page
5. Wix / WordPress / other (or don’t know)
6. Email or WhatsApp they actually check
7. Hours
8. Service area
9. What the visitor should leave (name, phone, what they need)
10. When we may edit
11. They create the login. We do not invent passwords. Or sit 20 min with Danny.

Visitor is never told they are booked. Text the pack to Danny 786-660-1778.

items.q: What is Lead Response?
items.a: When someone is on the shop’s website and they can’t pick up, that person leaves a name and a phone number. It hits the inbox or text the shop actually looks at. They’re not told they have an appointment. The shop calls them back. We put that on the site they already have, so it looks like their page. We stay until they’ve called a test one themselves. That’s the install. Seventy-five hundred, one time.

items.q: So it’s a form? A widget? A plugin? A chatbot?
items.a: No. A box that sits in a folder nobody opens is not this. This notifies the phone they actually look at, never tells the visitor they’re booked, keeps the same number from becoming two jobs, and we don’t leave until the shop called a test lead.

items.q: Is this a new website?
items.a: No. Walk if that’s what they want.

items.q: Do you answer the phone? Answering service? Call center? Virtual receptionist?
items.a: No. The shop calls. We are not the receptionist.

items.q: Ads? SEO? Google ranking? LSAs? Get us leads?
items.a: No. We catch people already on their site when they can’t pick up. You don’t need to buy ads for this SKU. If they want traffic, walk.

items.q: Does this replace Jobber / ServiceTitan / Housecall / HighLevel / their CRM?
items.a: No. This sits on the website they already have. We don’t take over the board they run jobs on.

items.q: Live chat? Facebook leads? Angi? HomeAdvisor? Thumbtack?
items.a: Those are other products. This is missed visitors on THEIR website.

items.q: How is this different from the contact page they already have?
items.a: Most contact pages sit in a folder nobody checks, or they auto-reply like the job is already booked. This hits the phone they actually look at, never books the visitor, and we stay until they called a test lead.

items.q: How is this different from Wix / Squarespace / WordPress contact or Google Forms?
items.a: Those don’t ring the phone they check, don’t stop a second job from the same number, don’t keep the visitor from thinking they’re booked, and nobody sits with them until a real callback happened. That’s why this is an install, not a template they forget.

items.q: Can they just do this themselves?
items.a: They’re welcome to try. This SKU is the install — on their live page, looking like their page, done when they called a test lead. If they want to build it themselves, walk. You are not there to teach them.

items.q: How long to install?
items.a: Once we have the numbered pack and they create the login — or we sit twenty minutes while they set it — we put it on a page they already had. Done when they call the test lead.

items.q: What do you actually put on their site?
items.a: An after-hours line on a page they already have: can’t reach us, leave name and phone. It looks like their page. The visitor is never told they’re booked.

items.q: Do you rebuild their whole site?
items.a: No. We work on a page they already had.

items.q: Will customers see VOIDD on the shop’s site?
items.a: No. It looks like the shop’s page.

items.q: English and Spanish?
items.a: Yes. Pack the language they use. We have a sixty-second Spanish pitch.

items.q: After hours only — or also when they’re on a job at 2pm?
items.a: Whenever they can’t pick up. Nights, weekends, on a roof. Pack the hours they give us.

items.q: They already pay an answering service.
items.a: This is the website, not their inbound phone line. People on the site still leave a name. The shop still calls. If they only wanted us to replace the answering service, walk.

items.q: They have a full-time person on the phones.
items.a: If nobody is missing work, this is a hard close. Prefer shops that miss after hours or while they’re on a job.

items.q: Multiple locations? Franchise? Twenty trucks?
items.a: This price is one website. Another location is another install. Don’t invent a chain discount unless Danny says.

items.q: Mobile app? Booking calendar? Online pay? Deposits?
items.a: No. Name and phone. They call. Walk if that’s the product they wanted.

items.q: Can visitors pick a time slot?
items.a: No. That sounds booked. They leave a name. The shop calls.

items.q: Photo upload? Video of the unit?
items.a: Not this SKU.

items.q: Do you text the visitor back automatically?
items.a: Don’t promise a paid text pipe to the visitor. We notify the shop. The shop calls.

items.q: Email, text, or WhatsApp — what does the shop get?
items.a: Whatever inbox they actually check. That’s collect line 6. Don’t invent a new number for them.

items.q: Same person submits twice?
items.a: Same phone is one job, not two.

items.q: Spam? Junk? Bots?
items.a: We don’t invent traffic. We catch people on their site. Don’t promise zero junk.

items.q: How fast does the shop see it?
items.a: Same visit. It should hit the phone they packed.

items.q: What if nobody at the shop touches it?
items.a: There’s a flag if it sits a day. They still have to call. We are not the receptionist.

items.q: Who owns the names?
items.a: The shop. Always. We are not selling their list.

items.q: Can they pause it? Slow season?
items.a: Yes. Pause, booked, lost, follow — that’s the owner card. Don’t uninstall as a sales trick.

items.q: Hours, service area, services?
items.a: Packed from what they told us. Don’t invent Miami-Dade if they said Broward.

items.q: How much?
items.a: Seventy-five hundred, one time. Not a monthly.

items.q: What’s in the $7,500?
items.a: The install on their existing site. Looks like their page. Hits the inbox they check. Visitor never told they’re booked. Same phone is one job. They can mark booked / lost / follow and pause. A flag if nobody touched it for a day. Hours, area, language as packed. Owner card. We stay until they called a test lead. Login they create.

items.q: Monthly fee? Hosting? We take over their Wix bill?
items.a: No monthly from us. They already have a site. They keep paying whoever they pay for that site.

items.q: Can we discount? Five thousand? Payment plan? Intro price?
items.a: No. One price. Don’t invent another.

items.q: Why so much? I saw a $49 widget.
items.a: This is an install on their live page, not a widget they forget. One check. If they want cheap, walk. Don’t argue a feature list.

items.q: Why not more? Why not $20k on the first call?
items.a: This is the SKU. Ten and twenty are later, same shop, separate close. Don’t mix. Don’t quote seventy-five thousand as in-house.

items.q: Card? Zelle? Check? Wire? Deposit to start?
items.a: Shop pays VOIDD after the install is accepted. Danny settles how. Don’t invent terms on the first call. Get the pack.

items.q: Refund if nobody leaves a name?
items.a: No lead-volume promise, so no ‘leads refund.’ If our install isn’t on their live page as sold, that’s on us to make true. Don’t write a guarantee on the call.

items.q: What if it stops working later?
items.a: If our work stops doing what we sold, we put it back. If they rebuild the whole website, that’s a new job.

items.q: How long is the warranty? Forever concierge?
items.a: If our install breaks, we put it back. Not a year of free site babysitting.
